problem.text: AI agents can retrieve company knowledge.

But how do they know
which version to trust?

The approved policy says 24 hours.
Slack says 48. The checklist still says 24.

ingestion.text:
n8n ingests three synthetic feeds
and validates their metadata.

governance.text:
The ledger tracks the evidence
and who owns the policy.

escalation-review.text:
In the Review Desk, Support compares
the approved policy with the Slack decision.

The newer decision opens a review.
The 24-hour policy stays in force.

The owner approves 48 hours.
Version two preserves the decision trail.

contribution.text:
A department owner can propose
a procedure in the same desk.

The form applies the taxonomy
and records the intended audience.
The submission waits for a separate steward.

pending-retrieval.text:
Before approval, the employee gets
no verified answer.

steward-approval.text:
The steward approves the submission
and publishes version one.

approved-retrieval.text:
The same question returns a cited version.
HTTP and MCP share this policy.

restricted-retrieval.text:
The employee gets no restricted
Security content or citations.

quality-report.text:
The quality report assigns old copies
and overdue reviews to owners.

ContextLedger. Reliable context,
governed by people, accessible to AI.
